text: Welcome to This is My Architecture. I'm Todd from AWS. Today we're in New York City and I'm joined by Lee from Advanced Local. Lee, welcome.
Thank you.
Can you tell us a little bit about what Advanced Local does and your team specifically?

Yes, we're a large media organization that owns newspapers and websites across the country and my team specifically is the group that connects all the business systems and makes sure it's as automated as possible.
Okay, so multiple systems, newspaper, websites, I'm thinking ad content creation.
Yep, and that's specifically what this workflow is all about is how that we get that creative information from the sales rep to the team that actually builds the ads and gets them on the website.
Okay, awesome. So let's dive right in here. It sounds like some of that information goes to Salesforce. Is there some type of workflow or what does it really become initiated at?

And at the point that that's been filled out by the sales rep and marked complete, that actually flows via trigger into our API gateway.

parse it to turn it into something that's standardized and usable and store it on our DynamoDB for all the ad data.

Yep, so that information then actually has to get to the design team that needs to work on it. Lambda functions. And all that information that we stored up here is actually what they use to kick off those and work through their different things like proofing and the actual ad creation process in their end systems, all the way to fulfilling the ads back onto the sites.

Okay, great. So it sounds like the workflow function really helped with pulling the information, a specific set of business logic to front end and be executed with the application that's hosted on S3.
And can you talk a little bit more about the user experience? I see Amazon Cognito here as well. Whenever I see that, I think security and authentication.

So that was a big piece that we added to make sure that everything that we had going on was backed by a good layer of security so that we don't have any unauthorized users, anybody coming in building ads just for fun.

So we use Cognito and the user pools to quickly set up a auth for them. And that also allows us to pass that information on down to other systems that need an individual user login without the user having to go in and log in multiple times.

So a simple, simple, single sign on. Sure. Secure login, fronting the mobile app. So it looks like the automation process that you guys have created at Advanced Local really helps with what was once a manual flow.
Can you talk a little bit about the productivity increases or gains that you've experienced?

Yeah, it's been a great, especially from the admin side, we went from, you know, 20 people having to maintain legacy systems and legacy integrations that were manual and tedious to a group of one or two people that actually go in, keep the routing information up to date, keep the credentials updated, whatever they need to do, all just by that front end system.

So save a ton of time and resources there. And from a creative user perspective, now instead of having to go in and manually add and build all these creative resources, they're able to just press a few buttons and it just works.

Wow, that's great. So reducing the number of resources that were needed for a process that is now automated and two different workflows with a number of different back end systems that now uses a common set of AWS microservices. Very, very creative.
